title: Configure Prometheus remote write to send metrics to Grafana Cloud

blocks.content: In this milestone, you add a `remote_write` block to your Prometheus configuration file, usually `prometheus.yml`. The Cloud Portal generates the block for you. It contains the `/api/prom/push` URL of your Grafana Cloud Metrics instance, your instance ID as the username, and an access policy token as the password.
To configure Prometheus to remote write to Grafana Cloud, complete the following steps:
Log in to the Cloud Portal at [grafana.com](https://grafana.com/auth/sign-in).
Under **Grafana Cloud** in the left navigation, click the name of your stack.

whenTrue.alt: Image of stack selected in the Grafana Cloud Portal

blocks.content: On the **Prometheus** card, click **Send Metrics**.

Scroll down the page until you locate the **Sending metrics with Prometheus** section.

This section contains the `remote_write` block that you'll add to your Prometheus configuration.

Just below the code sample, click **Generate now** to create an access policy token.

Prometheus uses this token as the `remote_write` password.

whenTrue.alt: Picture of Generate now link to create an access policy token

blocks.content:
On the **Create an API token** screen, enter a name for the token and click **Create token**.

The code sample now includes the token you just created. This is the only time the portal shows the token, so keep this page open until you've copied the block.
On the **Create an API token** screen, click **Close**.

Just below the code sample, click **Copy to clipboard**.

In the following steps, you add this block to the `prometheus.yml` file.
Log in to the machine on which Prometheus is installed, and open a terminal.

If your user can't write to the Prometheus configuration file, switch to one that can.

For example:

```
sudo su -
```

Open `prometheus.yml` in a text editor. On many Linux installations the file is in `/etc/prometheus`.

For example, with Vim, run:

```
vim /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
```

Scroll to the end of the file and paste the `remote_write` block you copied from the Cloud Portal.

In Vim, press `i` to start editing before you paste. The result looks like this, with your own values in place of the placeholders:

```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: <Your Metrics instance remote_write endpoint>
    basic_auth:
      username: <Your Metrics instance ID>
      password: <Your Cloud Access Policy token>
```

If the file already has a `remote_write` section, add the new entry to that list instead of adding a second `remote_write` key.

Save the file and exit the editor.

In Vim, press `Esc`, then type `:wq` and press `Enter`.

Restart Prometheus so it reads the new configuration.

For example, if Prometheus runs as a systemd service:

```
systemctl restart prometheus
```

After the restart, Prometheus starts pushing the samples it scrapes to Grafana Cloud.

Check that Prometheus restarted without errors:

```
systemctl status prometheus
```

If the service failed to start, the most common cause is a YAML indentation error in the block you pasted. Check the service logs with `journalctl -u prometheus` or in `/var/log/syslog`.
In the next milestone, you verify that your metrics are arriving in Grafana Cloud.
